rationale: RATIONALE — bugs_open/260 renderer half. THE DEFECT. RenderTemplateReportingMissing (component_library.go:965) executes a component template with Go text/template via executeGoTemplate (call_agent.go:1170). On ANY error it logs at Warn and silently falls back to a regex renderer written for HANDLEBARS syntax (component_library.go:1032-1057). That renderer substitutes {{.field}} but cannot execute {{if}}, {{range}} or {{end}}, so it emits well-formed HTML with every control directive left in and every field value already resolved. Values resolved plus directives surviving is the diagnostic fingerprint: generation worked, and no template engine did the rendering. WHY NOW. [MEASURED 2026-08-19 20:45Z, re-run today] 26 events, 7 domains, 25 work items, 2026-08-11 15:39Z to 2026-08-18 23:36Z, accelerating — 08-18 alone was 9 events across three domains. 24 of the 25 items are parked at needs_human_review. Three lanes hit it independently in one week on unrelated sites, including a greenfield build with no prior components at all. WHY THE COST WAS UNDER-READ. The bug file's headline said 'no live damage', from a sound measurement of STORED content: nothing broken has ever been persisted, because validate_content refuses the page first. Both halves re-verify today (0 of 1,789 page_components and 0 of 72 site_components leak a control directive, positive-controlled regex). But the defect's entire effect is that NOTHING IS STORED, so a census of stored rows reports it as harmless by construction — survivorship, not safety. What actually happens is that the page never exists while the pages that did build keep linking to it: loanzy.uk serves a 404 at /your-rights.html, remortgagecalculator.uk carries two dead nav links on every page it serves. AND THE PROTECTION IS NARROWER THAN THE BUG FILE STATES — two corrections this lane made, both to sentences a reviewer checks first. (a) The bug file's §5 says the page-BUILD path 'has no schema gate at all'. FALSE at HEAD: missingRequiredLLMFields has two callers, rerender_page_sections_action.go:396 and v3_site_actions.go:2386, the latter inside the build render step. The build path has a PRESENCE gate; what it lacks is the TYPE half — which is exactly why a present-but-mistyped field sails through, consistent with all 26 events. (b) 'The gate is why there is no live damage' is true of the page-BUILD path only. applyContentEdit (section_editor_actions.go:886) and applyComponentSwap (:996) render through the same seam, and updatePageComponentAfterEdit writes rendered_html straight to an already-live page; grepping that file for validate/unrendered returns one unrelated comment. Both editor sites do carry an `if rendered == ""` guard and it CANNOT FIRE for this defect, because the fallback returns mangled HTML rather than empty. That path is exercised: 271 content_rewrite/content_edit items, 117 complete, since 2026-04-08. So the correct risk statement is not 'no live damage is possible' but 'the ungated path has not yet been unlucky'. WHY DELETING THE FALLBACK IS SAFE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. Three independent zeros, each with a control that could have come out otherwise. (1) 0 of 251 active component templates fail to Parse. Parse is data-independent so no RenderContext replica is involved; the seven FuncMap names were extracted mechanically from executeGoTemplate rather than typed, because an undefined function is itself a parse error. Controls: an unclosed {{if}} must fail (it did), a valid nested template must pass (it did). So the fallback is never entered via a parse error — every occurrence is an EXECUTE error, i.e. a data type violation. (2) 0 of 1,778 stored sections fail to Execute against their own stored content_data. Faithful without a RenderContext replica because contextToInterfaceMap merges ContentData at the top level (component_library.go:1263-1268) and missingkey=zero makes absent site fields safe; conservative, not inflated — it cannot manufacture a failure from a missing site field. Controls: the bug's own A/B pair — a string where an array is ranged must fail, the coerced array-of-objects must render. Both fired. (3) 0 of 253 active components use the fallback's own dialect: no {{# handlebars blocks, no {{nav_items_html}}, no {{quick_links_html}}. Together: deleting the fallback changes the behaviour of nothing that currently works. WHAT THE CHANGE DOES NOT DO. It does not make any page that currently fails succeed. Those pages already fail — at validate_content, with 20 blockers that are a regex cap (FindAllString(html, 10)) rather than a measurement. What changes is that they fail at the component, immediately, with the real error ('range can't iterate over ...'), naming the field. SUCCESS CRITERION, stated so it cannot be misread: the build fails EARLY naming `branches`, NOT 'the page builds'. The 24 parked items still hold mistyped content; making them build is the WRITER half's job (copy_quality_two_stage lane, owner direction 2026-08-12). CONSTRAINT THE DESIGN MUST RESPECT. The owner has ruled all sites should be capable of having tools, and tool pages legitimately carry {{ }} literals in copy; one of the 26 recorded occurrences is exactly that shape. The design therefore contains NO output brace-scan at all: it fires exactly when text/template returns an error, so content that merely contains braces never touches it — the constraint satisfied structurally rather than by heuristic. This also argues AGAINST tightening checkUnrenderedTemplates: with the seam failing loud, no leaked HTML reaches that detector at all. A THIRTEENTH SEAM NOBODY HAD NAMED (found by this lane, recorded as §13g of the bug file). RenderTemplateWithMap (rerender_pages_actions.go:782) is a SECOND, independent Go template executor with no FuncMap and no missingkey=zero, returning "" at Warn on parse or execute error — and its caller does html = contactInfoRe.ReplaceAllString(html, renderedContactInfo), so an error DELETES the live contact block, which is worse than mangling it and leaves nothing for any detector to find. [MEASURED 2026-08-19] latent today (the one active contact-info component renders clean there, 2,453 bytes, probed with that seam's own configuration and controlled both ways: {{safe .x}} must fail there — it did, proving the probe faithful to the absent FuncMap — and a plain {{.email}} must pass — it did). But the trigger is one ordinary {{safe}}/{{default}}/{{isset}} edit away: those are normal everywhere else in this library and are a PARSE error here. Fixed in the same change (return the input HTML unchanged) because the two seams do not accept the same language and nothing says so. SCOPE AND REGISTRATION. Shared rendering plumbing, so: this council round before/alongside the commit, and a concept-register entry in the same commit that ships it (owner ruling 2026-07-28 §2, condition 2). No ordering constraint is claimed (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §2 — on a shared HEAD there is none to claim). Other consumers have been TOLD rather than merely measured (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §3): copy_quality_two_stage owns the stage-2 executor that renders through this seam and has a written notice naming what changes about its guarantee (CONTRIB_2026-08-19, committed); loanzy_uk_example_site and portfolio_positioning hold reproductions and have been told the fix is Go and inert until a roll. RFC_022 CONSUMER ENUMERATION for the one new opt-in key, run rather than asserted [MEASURED 2026-08-19 20:47Z]: across 198 active non-snapshot agent_definitions, scanning default_config, task_workflow, orchestrator_workflow and orchestration_workflow, ZERO name refuse_mistyped_llm_fields — and zero name its precedent refuse_dead_url_controls either, so the new key arrives in the same state as the shape the owner ruled on. Unsafe side is the default-OFF side. By the RFC_022 ruling of 2026-08-11 that makes it not architecture-scope. COVERAGE HONESTY, stated because a green gate is not fleet coverage: 107 of the 110 exposed components carry a `fields` schema the checker can read, but 75 of 253 active components declare no schema at all, and for those the type gate is silent by construction. The hard error at the seam — not the gate — is the complete detector.

plan.summary: Delete the regex fallback and give the component render seam an error channel, so a component render either executed or errored and there is no third state. Every one of the fifteen call sites then makes an explicit, reviewed failure decision (fail the step on the build path; carry the stored HTML on the repair path; refuse the store on chrome; refuse the edit on the two ungated live-edit paths; take the existing fallback ladder on chrome injection). A new pure checker, datahelpers.ContentTypeViolations, supplies the actionable diagnosis: unconditionally as an ENRICHER on a render that has already failed (it adds no authority, firing only on failure), and as an opt-in pre-render refusal (key refuse_mistyped_llm_fields, default OFF) on the two gated paths. Ranked by what makes the bad state unrepresentable: (1) the seam can no longer emit output it did not execute; (2) each caller's failure behaviour is explicit and in the diff; (3) the type gate makes the failure earlier and named. The compile-breaking signature is deliberate — the rejected alternative, keeping RenderTemplate(...) string and returning "" on error, is a SECOND silent shape (assembleComponents would stitch a page missing a section; GateConvertedTemplate would gate an empty render), and it would hide the very call-site decisions this council needs to see. THREE FURTHER CALL SITES ARE IN THIS CHANGE BUT HAVE NO EDIT SLOT (the schema caps edits at 8; saying so rather than letting them read as uncovered): assemble_from_library.go:297 — fail the step, no writer data is in scope so an execute error means a corrupt template and a silently missing section is the bugs_open/018 class; component_instance_conversion.go:271 (GateConvertedTemplate) — propagate, so the RFC_034 acceptance gate refuses a template the real renderer cannot execute, which today it can green-light; cmd/component-render-check/rendercheck.go:653,680 — the offline audit, where the baseline render error routes to the existing `unanalysed` bucket AND the per-field probe error must be recorded rather than counted as a clean probe (an errored probe renders "" and would otherwise SILENCE findings — the detector-blinding class), with baseline noise verified by a live run before commit.

edits.rationale: The seam itself. On executeGoTemplate error, return the wrapped error instead of the regex fallback — executeGoTemplate's error already carries line, field and offending value ('range can't iterate over "..."'). The three chrome renderers propagate that error into a ladder that ALREADY handles it: InjectHeader:2141, InjectFooter:2186 and InjectHead:2349 each answer err != nil with RenderFallbackHeader/Footer/Head today, so chrome needs error PLUMBING, not new mechanism. Deleting the fallback also removes contextToMap, whose two remaining members fabricate URLs (primary_cta_url -> /contact.html, secondary_cta_url -> /about.html) — bugs_open/203's residue — but ONLY because RenderTemplateWithValidation, its other caller, is dead and dies in the same commit.

The build path, where 25 of the 26 recorded events flow. Fail the step in the same shape as the missingRequiredLLMFields refusal twenty lines above (:2379-2394) and the dead-URL refusal just below, so the parked work item carries the CAUSE rather than 20 capped symptoms. Also the first of the two sites where the type checker runs: as an unconditional enricher on the already-failed error, and as the opt-in pre-render refusal.

The repair vehicle. Carry the stored HTML on a render error using this path's OWN existing carried-section machinery (carryStoredSection, four existing carry branches at :446-487) — never replace good stored bytes with a failed render, and never fail the whole page, which would deadlock the path's own remedy. Named in the diagnostic rather than only logged, for exactly the bugs_open/182 reason the other carries cite: a re-render in which every section takes a carry branch is otherwise indistinguishable from one that worked.

PLUS `RenderFailedSlots []string` on rerenderResolution (:788-799) surfaced as out["carried_render_failed"] beside carried_not_ready/carried_empty_template, and named in describe(). NON-FATAL by design — fatal() keeps its current membership (UnresolvedSlots, InvalidTemplateSlots), because a repair re-render that refuses on the state it was dispatched to fix deadlocks its own remedy; stated in the comment rather than left to be rediscovered. PLUS refuse_mistyped_llm_fields declared on RerenderPageSectionsInputSpec, armed the same way (default OFF).

edits.rationale: The chrome STORE path, which has no gate downstream — whatever it stores is what the site serves. On a render error do NOT store: the existing row keeps serving, which is strictly better than replacing working chrome with mangled chrome. A first build with no existing row is the one case that must fail the step instead: a site must not go live with a silently missing chrome slot. Note the existing `if renderedHTML == ""` guard at :928 cannot fire for this defect today, because the fallback returns mangled HTML rather than empty.

edits.rationale: The two UNGATED live-page routes — this is the hole the rationale's correction (b) is about. updatePageComponentAfterEdit writes rendered_html straight to an already-live page with no validate_content between, and the existing `if rendered == ""` guard at :887 and :997 provably cannot fire for this defect because the fallback returns mangled HTML, never empty. Returning the error refuses the edit and leaves the live row untouched, which is the same choice the build path makes and the only one that closes the route.

The THIRTEENTH SEAM, found by this lane and in no prior document. RenderTemplateWithMap is a second, independent executor with no FuncMap and no missingkey=zero that returns "" at Warn, and its caller ReplaceAllStrings the LIVE contact-info block with that "" — so an error DELETES the section, leaving nothing for any detector to find. Returning the input HTML unchanged is the smallest correct behaviour: a failed contact-info re-render must leave the block that is already serving. The legacy whole-page head render at :532 takes the existing fallback-head else-branch, which the function already has.
edits.sketch:
- renderedContactInfo := RenderTemplateWithMap(htmlTemplate, templateData, logger)
- html = contactInfoRe.ReplaceAllString(html, renderedContactInfo)
+ renderedContactInfo, err := RenderTemplateWithMap(htmlTemplate, templateData, logger)
+ if err != nil {
+   // Do not delete a live block because a render failed. This seam has no
+   // FuncMap and no missingkey=zero, so an ordinary {{safe}}/{{default}}/
+   // {{isset}} — normal everywhere else in this library — is a PARSE error
+   // HERE and used to blank the section (bugs_open/260 §13g).
+   logger.Error("contact-info re-render failed — leaving the existing block in place", zap.Error(err))
+   return html

func RenderTemplateWithMap(...) (string, error): parse and execute errors return ("", err) instead of ("", nil) at Warn; the missingBareFields report and <no value> strip are unchanged on the success path.
HEAD at :532: `renderedHead := RenderTemplate(headTemplate, renderCtx, logger)` becomes `renderedHead, err := ...; if err != nil { logger.Error(...); headTemplate = "" /* take the existing fallback-head else-branch */ }` — no new mechanism, the else-branch already builds a complete head.

edits.rationale: The actionable diagnosis, as a pure function beside SchemaContentFields so it is testable with no DB and no render. RECURSION INTO `items` IS MANDATORY, not a refinement: the live case is a NESTED violation (steps[2].branches), so a top-level-only check would miss the very instance that motivated the change. Deliberately conservative — absent, nil and empty are NEVER violations, unknown or undeclared types are skipped rather than guessed, and only source:"llm" fields are examined because resolver fills already have resolvedValueSatisfiesDeclaredType (render_site_components_action.go:865) as their live precedent for refusing a declared-type violation.
edits.sketch:
type TypeViolation struct{ Path, Declared, Actual string } // e.g. {"steps[2].branches", "array (items: object)", "string"}
func ContentTypeViolations(schema map[string]interface{}, content map[string]interface{}) []TypeViolation
Rules: declared type IN ('array','list') — `list` is real, 5 live fields — and value present, non-nil, non-[] => must be []interface{}; an `items` block declaring object shape => every element must be map[string]interface{}, recursing for nested arrays and carrying the index in Path; absent/nil/empty => no violation; unknown or absent declared type => skipped; non-llm-sourced fields => skipped. Nil schema => nil.
DescribeTypeViolations renders them one per line for a log field and an error suffix.
TWO MODES WITH DIFFERENT AUTHORITY, and the split is the point: (1) ENRICHER, unconditional, at the build and rerender sites, appended to an error the RENDER already returned — it fires only on failure so it adds no authority and needs no key; (2) PRE-RENDER REFUSAL, opt-in via refuse_mistyped_llm_fields, default OFF, because the checker keys on SCHEMA not on the template, so a mistyped field the template never references builds fine today and refusing it unconditionally would be NEW AUTHORITY OVER CONTENT THAT CURRENTLY RENDERS — the 2026-08-02 §2 ruling exactly, with dead_url_guard.go's own history (three seats independently demanded default-OFF for this shape) as the local precedent. Arming migration sql_for_agents/NNN_bugfix_260_arm_type_gate_HOLD.sql patterned on 380, asserting the step count so a future third render step fails loudly; image first, then seed.

plan.risks: 1) THE SIGNATURE CHANGE BREAKS EVERY CALLER BY DESIGN — that is the review surface, but it means the change cannot be partial: 15 non-test call sites plus 8 test files must land in one commit or HEAD does not compile, and HEAD is shared (any other session's make build-* ships it). Mitigation: build with `git archive HEAD` before pushing, and the commit is one coherent task. 2) THE OFFLINE AUDIT CAN BE BLINDED BY ITS OWN FIX: rendercheck's per-field probe deliberately REMOVES a field and renders; under the new seam that render can now ERROR where it previously produced fallback output, and an errored probe renders "" whose shapeCounts are zero — i.e. it would read as 'this field is clean'. The probe error must therefore be recorded in its own bucket, never counted as a clean probe, and baseline noise must be measured by a live run BEFORE commit (predicted zero — predict then measure). 3) CHROME BEHAVIOUR CHANGES ON A FAILING RENDER from 'mangled chrome ships' to 'fallback chrome ships' (Inject*) or 'the existing row keeps serving' (store). Fallback chrome is visibly plainer; a reviewer should confirm that is preferable to shipping directives — this lane says yes, and the marker comment makes it greppable rather than mysterious. 4) THE RERENDER CARRY IS NON-FATAL, so a page whose sections all fail to render re-saves its stored HTML and reports carried_render_failed rather than failing — deliberate (it is the repair vehicle) but it means the rerender path alone cannot escalate this defect; the build path and the audit are what escalate it. 5) THE TYPE GATE IS SILENT FOR 75 OF 253 ACTIVE COMPONENTS (no schema at all), and 3 of the 110 exposed ones; a green gate must never be reported as fleet coverage, which is why the register entry states the caveat. 6) DELETING contextToMap removes bugs_open/203's two fabricate-a-URL members as a side effect — an improvement, but it is a behaviour change on any template that relied on primary_cta_url/secondary_cta_url appearing from nowhere; measured 0 such templates, and the fabricated values were the fossil the 203 lane wants gone. 7) The arming migration must not be applied until an image carrying this change has rolled (image first, then seed) — it is named _HOLD for that reason. 8) A same-file passenger risk this lane cannot control: rerender_page_sections_action.go is currently dirty in the shared tree with another lane's 26-line comment block (council 060bcc0a r5), and a pathspec commit takes a same-file passenger; it will be named in the commit message rather than pretended away.
